architecture: implementations/go/README.md:62-90 — the documented pipeline (lexer → parser → analyzer → optimizer → physical → exec) maps one-to-one onto packages under internal/ (sql/lexer, sql/parser, analyzer, plan, optimizer, physical, exec, storage, pqcf, index, catalog, ingest, protocol, server, native, errs). Each package has a single stated responsibility.

internal/engine/engine.go:440-466 — plan() is a thin facade: analyzer.AnalyzeQuery → optimizer.Optimize → physical.Build. Each stage gets an Options struct, and dependencies are injected (EvalConst: exec.EvalConstant, Indexes: snap.IndexesOf), so the optimizer and planner do not import exec state.

internal/optimizer/optimizer.go:28 — a Rule interface with ordered, individually switchable rules split by file (fold.go, pushdown.go, reorder.go, prune.go). internal/physical/planner.go:node is the only place that makes execution decisions, as the README states.

README 'Column IDs instead of positions' plus internal/plan/expr.go — expressions use statement-unique ColumnIDs that are resolved to positions only when exec compiles them, so rewrite rules stay decoupled from physical layouts. Catalog is copy-on-write with immutable snapshots (engine.go:441).
readability: internal/sql/parser/parser.go:1-80,525-733 — a textbook recursive-descent parser: one small method per precedence level (orExpr/andExpr/notExpr/predicate/additive/multiplicative/unary/primary) and tiny helpers (peek/accept/expect) that attach line/column to errors.

internal/exec/parallel.go:15-28 — a long comment explaining why morsel ordering and first-failing-morsel error reporting keep parallel results identical to serial execution. internal/storage/table.go:101 and engine.go:66-70 likewise document intent in their comments.

internal/exec/vexpr.go:1034-1150 (evalDict, ~117 lines) and vagg.go (1240 lines), vexpr.go (1113 lines), vops.go/vsort.go (~700 lines each) — the vectorized layer is dense, with large files and long functions full of type-specialized branches, so it is harder to follow than the rest.
Idiomatic Go throughout: errors returned as values, Options structs, generics where useful (gather[T] in parallel.go:246), standard library only (go.mod has no requirements).
robustness: internal/protocol/handler.go:116-134 — guard() recovers panics into INTERNAL_ERROR responses with a logged stack, and errs.From maps every error to a stable code. server/server.go:620-627 and stream.go:127 do the same for streamed queries. internal/errs/errs.go:14-38 mirrors all spec error codes and attaches line/column details to parse errors.

internal/engine/engine.go:159-199 — path safety rejects absolute paths, NUL, '..' and backslash roots with ACCESS_DENIED. readFile checks the ingestion limit with Stat and then again with an io.LimitReader. server.go:99,319 adds ReadHeaderTimeout and a LimitReader on request bodies. server/admission.go:38 uses a bounded queue that returns OVERLOADED.

internal/pqcf/read.go:96-136,358-706 — thorough validation of untrusted PQCF files: magic, version, flags, metadata length range, CRC on metadata and on each chunk, UTF-8, decreasing string offsets, dictionary code range, zero-length and over-covering RLE runs, trailing bytes, non-finite floats, row-count resource limit. Lazy chunks keep their decode error (storage/table.go:101-112).

Gaps: exec/parallel.go:249 and exec/vagg.go:1081,1096 start worker goroutines with no recover, so a panic in a worker kills the whole process because guard() covers only the calling goroutine. protocol/session.go:13-16 uses ReadBytes('\n') with no per-line size cap. sql/parser/parser.go has no expression nesting-depth limit. native/native.go:124-128 turns short buffers into a panic rather than an error.
testability: 23 _test.go files, about 4,050 test lines against about 26,800 lines of production code (roughly 15%). Every layer has its own unit tests: parser_test, analyzer_test, optimizer_test, physical_test/access_test, exec_test/simd_test, pqcf_test, types/widedecimal_test, catalog/index/storage/ingest tests, protocol_test, server_test.

internal/optimizer/optimizer_test.go:19-50 — a clean harness: logical() parses and analyzes against shared testutil fixtures, and apply() runs any subset of rules, compares plan.Format output and asserts the rules did not mutate their input plan. Adding a rule test takes a few lines.

internal/exec/exec_test.go:11-60 — table-driven tests for LIKE, SUBSTR, case mapping and ROUND. internal/engine/modes_test.go (355 lines) cross-checks the row, vectorized and parallel modes, and server_test.go tests admission control and streaming with fakes.

Weakness: the vectorized and parallel executor (about 6,000 lines across vagg/vexpr/vops/vsort/vjoin/parallel) is covered only by a 114-line exec_test.go and simd_test.go at the unit level. It relies mostly on engine-level mode-comparison tests and the external conformance harness.

top_strengths: Very clean layering with one package per pipeline stage, ColumnID-based plan rewrites, an injectable rule-based optimizer and a separate physical planner, all documented in the README module map
Thorough, defensive PQCF reader with checksums, range checks on offsets, dictionary codes and RLE runs, and resource limits
Consistent structured error model (errs.Code mirrors the spec) with panic-to-INTERNAL_ERROR guards at the protocol and HTTP boundaries, plus admission control, timeouts and body limits
Standard library only, idiomatic Go, with comments that explain why (parallel determinism, dictionary immutability)
top_weaknesses: Worker goroutines in parallel scan, aggregation and merge (exec/parallel.go:249, exec/vagg.go:1081,1096) have no recover, so any panic there crashes the whole server or session
Vectorized executor files are very large (vagg.go 1240 lines, vexpr.go 1113 lines) with long type-specialized functions (evalDict about 117 lines), which hurts readability
Unbounded inputs remain: no size cap on session lines (protocol/session.go:16) and no parser recursion-depth limit
Thin direct unit tests for the vectorized and parallel executor compared with its size
